David Vélez on why stablecoins could save the US dollar:

"There are about 190 currencies around the world. My view is that in 10-20 years from now, those 190 will be 10.

The fiscal situation in so many countries around the world is so dire that a lot of that fiat money is not real money. 

And so increasingly, billions of people are going to be banking on the offshore world, US stablecoin, but also Bitcoin and other type of assets.

I think the US stablecoins ultimately will be the big savior or one of the biggest saviors of the US dollar, because it democratizes access to the US dollar.

At least there is a lot of demand for the US stablecoin. There's very little for the Brazilian stablecoin, unfortunately."

#Uranium #Silver #Copper #Gold
⚡ DAILY METALS PULSE | 14 October 2026
Hotter US inflation hit precious metals today as the dollar and Treasury yields climbed. A reminder: inflation can hurt precious metals initially when markets respond by pricing in higher interest rates. A bit longer-term the story is different.

☢️ URANIUM
Fresh signs of nuclear expansion: Bluecore Energy announced a low-enriched uranium purchase for its maritime reactor programme, while Westinghouse placed conditional component orders for Poland’s first nuclear plant.

My take: fuel procurement and equipment orders make the nuclear growth story increasingly tangible. The demand implications build over years.

🥈 SILVER
Spot silver fell around 6.6% to $55.53/oz in Reuters’ late-session update. A brutal move that underlines silver’s volatility when the macro backdrop turns against precious metals. Watch whether buyers return as the dollar settles.

🔌 COPPER
A striking imbalance: Comex warehouses now hold roughly 70% of globally visible copper inventories, according to Reuters. Tariff fears pulled metal into the US, tightening availability elsewhere.

Location matters. A large US stockpile can coexist with shortages in other markets. Tariff decisions remain a major price catalyst.

🥇 GOLD
Spot gold fell around 1.8% to $4,084/oz. Higher yields are the immediate headwind; central-bank demand and concerns over government debt remain longer-term supports.

👀 NEXT WATCH
The dollar, Treasury yields, Fed commentary and copper positioning ahead of LME Week.

My view: stay selective. Today shows how quickly macro pressure can overwhelm a longer-term metals thesis.

#Uranium #Nuclear $SYH $SYHBF

Skyharbour’s next few months could be pivotal, and this webinar shows why. 👇

CEO Jordan Trimble and VP Exploration Serdar Donmez break down the company’s largest annual drill campaign: 30,000+ metres across its portfolio, with roughly 25,000 metres focused on Moore and Russell Lake. Assays are pending, with results expected to generate news flow into 2027.

⚛️ Denison is putting money into the ground. Approximately 3,600 metres of drilling has commenced at Getty East, funded by Denison under its earn-in agreement. This forms part of the planned 15,000+ metres across the Russell Lake area in 2026.

🎯 Location could make a discovery especially valuable. Management highlights Sphinx, roughly 700 metres from Denison’s Phoenix deposit, among the upcoming Wheeler North targets. Existing infrastructure and that proximity add strategic appeal.

💎 Moore remains 100% owned. Previous drilling returned 11.77% U₃O₈ over 1.6 metres, within 4.84% over 4.4 metres. Further exploration is testing extensions, basement targets and the Nomad corridor.

🤝 Partners multiply the exploration effort. Eleven partners across 14 projects represent more than C$130 million in potential combined consideration, assuming completion of their earn-ins.

🇺🇸 A potential Nasdaq listing adds another catalyst. Trimble’s realistic timing is Q1 2027, subject to completing the listing process.

My thesis: high-grade exploration, strategic partners and multiple opportunities for discovery give Skyharbour compelling upside as the uranium cycle develops.

Disclosure: Paid partnership with Skyharbour Resources. Please do your own research.

tweets.text:
In the drawdown from last year’s highs, SUI fell about 80%, SOL about 70%, ETH about 60%. Brutal.

But the charts missed what was underneath. On all three, economic density didn’t move. Users left, as they always do in a bear market, but the capital each remaining user had deployed stayed exactly where it was... the tourists and the bots went, and the people who stayed kept doing what they’d been doing.

I spent a lot of time measuring this: stablecoin float, DeFi TVL and applications shipped per daily user, across every major L1. Why? Because I think it’s the truest measure of longevity there is.

Every other L1 I measured lost density along with price. Adoption hadn’t taken hold yet. Doesn’t mean it won’t, but it hasn’t...

i wanted a physical version of my ai agent. Something real in the living room that shows my to-do list and my day, and that my wife can see too.

I bought a seeed reterminal e1002, an e-ink display. e-ink because it looks like paper: no glow, no buzz, it just sits there like a note on the wall (almost)

setup was honestly simple:
- built the open-source muse gadget firmware on my computer with my sdk token in it
- flashed it to the device over usb
- paired it in the muse app (settings, devices, developer mode) thanks @natfriedman 

now every morning at 7am my agent renders my briefing (calendar, top to-dos, weather) and pushes it to the screen. my wife reads it over coffee. it basically became the family's shared to-do list

whole thing took ~20 min. your agent doesn't have to live in a chat window. give it a physical representation!
